name: Lake Garda
title: Holidays in Lake Garda
intro: Lake beaches, ferries between pretty towns and Italy's biggest theme park. Here's what Lake Garda is like with the family, when to go and how long to stay.
facts_note: The EU is bringing in new entry checks, so check the rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: May, June and September are perfect, with warm days and room on the beaches. July and August are hot and lively. Many hotels, ferries and attractions close from November to March.

things.name: Gardaland
things.blurb: Italy's biggest theme park, with rides for all ages and an aquarium next door.

things.name: Lake ferries
things.blurb: Hop between lakeside towns by boat. A day pass makes it easy.

things.name: Sirmione
things.blurb: A castle surrounded by water, Roman ruins and the best gelato on the lake.

things.name: Monte Baldo cable car
things.blurb: A rotating cable car from Malcesine to mountain meadows high above the lake.

things.name: Lake beaches
things.blurb: Pebbly beaches with clear water and gentle shelving, good for little swimmers.

things.name: Verona
things.blurb: A Roman arena and Juliet's balcony, about 30 minutes away.

faqs.question: Is Lake Garda good for a family holiday?
faqs.answer: Yes. It's an easy mix of swimming, theme parks and mountains, with lots of campsites and family hotels. There are no waves, which suits young children.

faqs.question: How many nights do you need?
faqs.answer: A week is typical. Pick a base in the south for theme parks or in the north for mountains and watersports.

faqs.question: Do UK families need a visa?
faqs.answer: No, British passport holders can visit for up to 90 days in any 180 without a visa. New EU entry checks are being brought in, so check GOV.UK before you travel.

faqs.question: Do you need a car?
faqs.answer: It helps, but the ferries and buses link the main towns. Verona airport is about 30 minutes from the south of the lake.
